# 1 Clement Chapter 35 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 35

**35:1** How blessed and wonderful are the gifts of God, beloved! Life in immortality, brightness in righteousness, truth in boldness, faith in confidence, self-control in holiness; and all these fall within our comprehension.

**35:2** What then are the things prepared for those who wait for him? The Creator and Father of the ages, the All-holy One, knows their greatness and beauty.

**35:3** Let us therefore strive earnestly to be found in the number of those who wait for him, that we may receive a share of the gifts he has promised.

**35:4** But how shall this be, beloved? If our mind is fixed on God through faith; if we seek out what is pleasing and acceptable to him; if we accomplish what belongs to his blameless will; and if we follow the way of truth, casting far from us all unrighteousness and wickedness, covetousness, strife, malice and deceit, whispering and slander, hatred of God, pride and arrogance, vainglory and want of hospitality.

**35:5** For those who practice these things are hateful to God; and not only those who do them, but also those who approve of them.

**35:6** For the scripture says: "But to the sinner God said: Why do you recite my statutes and take my covenant upon your lips?

**35:7** Yet you hated instruction and cast my words behind you. When you saw a thief you ran along with him, and with adulterers you kept company. Your mouth was full of wickedness, and your tongue wove deceit. You sat and spoke against your brother, and you laid a stumbling block against your mother's son.

**35:8** These things you did and I kept silent; you thought, O wicked one, that I would be like you. I will convict you and lay the charge before your face.

**35:9** Understand this, you who forget God, lest he seize you like a lion, with none to deliver you.

**35:10** The sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and that is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God."

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 35 moves from eschatological promise (vv. 1-3) to the conditions of participation (v. 4 vice-list) to warning (vv. 5-10). The Psalm 50 LXX (49 LXX) citation is the longest in this section and is directed at hypocrites who mouth God's law while living contrary to it. The application to the Corinthian schismatics — who presumably still practiced Christian worship — is pointed. The final verse (35:10) echoes Psalm 50:23 LXX and provides the resolution: genuine worship (*sacrifice of praise*) is what honors God, not liturgical performance divorced from holy living. Romans 1:32 ("not only those who do them but those who approve") may be echoed in v. 5.

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus translation, balancing literalness and clarity.*
